title: Hierarchical Quantum Transport from Coupled Topological Domain-Wall States in SSH Chains
authors: Alessio Palavicini, César G. Galván, Carlos Ramírez
abstract: We investigate the transport properties of Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains containing multiple topological domain walls and show that their interaction generates a hierarchy of emergent spectral structures. Each domain wall contributes a localized state inside the SSH gap, and the hybridization of these states produces minibands whose signatures are directly reflected in the transmission spectra. By combining domain-wall lattices with different domain-wall separations, we construct effective SSH structures within the miniband subspace. The resulting transmission spectra reproduce the characteristic features of conventional SSH chains, including gap formation, finite-size resonances, and the correspondence between transmission spectra and band structure. The construction can be applied recursively, generating successive generations of effective SSH structures. As a consequence, effective SSH spectra repeatedly emerge within progressively narrower energy intervals, producing a self-similar hierarchy of minibands and spectral gaps. To understand the origin of this hierarchy, we develop an effective renormalized description based on successive decimation. The effective parameters exhibit a hierarchy of interlaced singularities whose number increases at each iteration. These singularities partition the energy axis into progressively finer intervals and provide a natural interpretation of the repeated fragmentation of the spectrum. Our results show that topological domain-wall states can act as emergent degrees of freedom from which multiscale transport channels, effective couplings, and hierarchical spectral structures may be engineered. More generally, the framework introduced here establishes a connection between recursive topological constructions, effective Hamiltonians, and the emergence of self-similar spectra in one-dimensional systems.
summary: This work explores quantum transport in SSH chains containing topological domain walls, showing that their interaction creates a self-similar hierarchy of minibands. By developing a recursive construction and analyzing the system via successive decimation, the authors demonstrate how localized topological states act as emergent degrees of freedom to engineer complex, multiscale spectral features. This establishes a general connection between recursive topological building blocks and self-similar spectral organization in 1D quantum systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates how the interaction of topological domain-wall states in Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chains generates a self-similar, hierarchical structure in quantum transport properties.
main_result: The hybridization of domain-wall localized states leads to minibands whose structure can be recursively constructed, revealing a self-similar hierarchy of spectral gaps and resonances.
method: The analysis combines the recursive scattering-matrix method with the development of an effective renormalized description based on successive decimation procedures.
model_or_system: The system is based on SSH chains containing multiple topological domain walls. The model is analyzed by treating the domain-wall states as emergent degrees of freedom that define an effective, recursively built lattice structure.
key_observables: Transmission spectra, minibands, spectral gaps, and the hierarchy of interlaced singularities in the energy axis.
important_parameters: Dimerization parameter (delta), number of domain walls ($N_d$), and the recursive generation index ($n$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the recursive nature of the scattering-matrix method and the mathematical validity of the decimation procedure for generating effective parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the formation of domain-wall lattices, the resulting transmission spectra for increasing domain-wall numbers, and the recursive rules generating higher-order structures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the initial SSH model with domain walls to demonstrating the recursive construction of effective SSH structures within minibands, culminating in a rigorous mathematical analysis of the singularity generation via successive decimation.
why_interesting: The concept of emergent, self-similar spectral structures arising from simple local topological defects provides a powerful, general framework for understanding multiscale physics in low-dimensional quantum systems.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: (a) Finite Su-Shrieffer-Heeger model with hopping amplitudes v and w and length Nw = 5. (b) Transmittance and dispersion of SSH chains with: (Left) Fixed δ = 0.4 and Nw = 1, 5 and 12, and (Right) Fixed length Nw = 12, and δ = 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. The number of transmission resonances increases with chain length, while the gap width is controlled by the dimerization parameter.

Figure 2: Formation of minibands from coupled domain-wall states. (a) Domain-wall lattice ob- tained by concatenating SSH chains. The red dashed lines indicate the domain-wall positions. (b) Transmission spectra for increasing numbers of domain walls Nd and the corresponding band structures of the associated infinite periodic sys- tems. Hybridization of the localized domain-wall states produces minibands embedded within the original SSH gap. The cases Nw = 1 and Nw = 2 generate three-band and five-band spectra, respec- tively.

Figure 3: (a) First-generation building blocks W (1) and V (1), corresponding to N(1) W = 1 and M(1) W = 2, respectively. The lower schematic illustrates the construction of an effective SSH chain from alternating V (1) and W (1) blocks. (b) Transmission spectra for effective SSH chains with NW = 1, 2, and 5, together with the band structure of the corresponding infinite periodic sequence. Calculations were performed for δ = 0.4.

Figure 4: Hierarchical SSH structures and their transmission spectra. Hierarchy levels are shown from left to right and their corresponding progressive amplifications from top to bottom. Boxes: Effective SSH building blocks of an arbitrary hierarchical level n.

Figure 5: Effective renormalized description of domain-wall lattices. (a) Elementary three-site decimation. (b) Iterative reduction of a finite SSH segment containing Nw hopping amplitudes w. (c) Effective periodic chain obtained after replacing each SSH segment by its renormalized counterpart. (d) Effective parameters for the elementary domain-wall lattice with Nw = 1. (e) Effective parameters for the elementary domain-wall lattice with Nw = 2. Red dashed curves correspond to the effective hopping t(Nw), while cyan solid curves denote the effective site energy ε(Nw). Green segments mark the energies satisfying the effective band condition, Eq. (17).
